Based on the reviews here I bought one and I'm glad I did!

This VCR/DVD was an early Christmas present to myself after deciding to join the rest of the world in DVD-land but not wanting to let go of my VHS movies quite yet. Based on the reviews and price, and because I own a JVC TV, this was my choice. I agree with the easy set-up. It's a bit awkward to work the whole TV/VHS/DVD selection options but I think I've gotten the hang of it.Two comments: it's not intuitive and actually is pretty complicated (too many buttons on the remote but that might please others who are more technically-minded than me) so I've had to rely heavily on the how-to manual. And setting the VCR timer is awkward -- you can't enter the start and end time but have to scroll (unless I'm missing something)...but those are my only complaints. This is a good product for your $$$.

A solid, tactical shooter at its core and certainly worth thinking about buying, even at full price. There's plenty of enjoyment to be had. That being said the enjoyment mostly comes from the interaction with other players rather than the game itself.  Many games are like that though and deserve a recommendation. 

I can't recommend Squad when the game changes what it wants to be every few years whilst breaking parts / failing to fix parts of the game. Ignoring the server browser issues, because who wants to find a server consistently, the most egregious problem for me has been the change to the vehicle physics. Many vehicles have a horrendous driving experience, and for what reason exactly? The game far too often goes from something that works to something different whilst breaking stuff in the process. It's incredibly frustrating. If it weren't for those 'Only in Battlefield' player moments, I wouldn't bother coming back.

Just Okay

This book is 'just okay.' I came away from reading the book not knowing too much about the Amish. Sue prefers to keep most of the information to herself. She does, however, make sure she gets in adequate writing about all of her 'accomplishments' -- and makes apparent her desire to return to her old life of those accomplishments. (Big hairy deal!) Personally I think she's a bore....and a boor; actually I found her to be pompous. She had a wonderful idea which could have been made better. Sue Bender, you need to grow up.

I used to love this game. Elite Dangerous was once one of the best space simulators ever made.

I still remember the wonder I felt the first time I launched into space, jumping from system to system, staring at the full explorable galaxy map, and setting off on long voyages into the vast unknown. I played as a hauler, moving goods from one location to another. It was simple, but deeply fulfilling. As I built my reputation, I earned better parts, more cargo space, better ships, higher payouts, and the ability to travel to distant systems.

Back then, the progression felt rewarding. I remember starting with tiny payouts of only a few thousand credits, and by the end of my last playthrough a few years ago, I was earning millions per mission. It felt like my time and effort mattered.

I recently reinstalled the game hoping to relive that nostalgia, but unfortunately, I was very disappointed. This once-beloved game has become painfully grindy. Now even allied factions only seem to offer a couple hundred thousand credits instead of the millions they used to. Many of the missions require you to spend credits to purchase or locate goods yourself, which takes away from the simple hauling

There's plenty to love about this game, but also plenty to hate. It's ruined for me by god awful back tracking, no fast travel, too many loading screens, genuinely awful music, janky controls. If you really love RPGs and space stuff, you'll probably like it. And there's a lot I do like, but damn there are some really terrible and baffling design choices here. 

Things I like:
- Ship designs are cool
- RPG mechanics are solid
- Space combat is pretty fun 
- Runs pretty well
- Graphics are pretty good

Things I don't like:
- Music is genuinely so terrible. turned it off an hour in
- Story is mid
- Control schemes involve a lot of adjusting on controller
- Annoying conversations happening that dont let you dock or give you the next mission so you have to just fly in circles and wait for it to finish with no way to skip
- Back tracking SUCKS it's absolutely horrendous and there is a ton of it necessary in game. Your home base is in the first star system and there are a handful of them that open up as the game goes on. If you are in, say the fourth system and need to return to your base, the process is a pain. Starting in the fourth system, you first have to fly into space (loading screen),

Lately, it's been a little flat -- both in terms of magazine size and in the depth of the articles. I'm renewing it one more year and hope it improves during that time

Disgrace of a book for anyone who studies the Amish writings

2 stars is pretty generous, in my opinion. This book seemed more like a book about the process she went through writing a book about visiting Amish families. I found myself wondering where I might be able to find the book she spent so much time "pouring her soul into". The book is largely spent talking about how incredible she is for having completed such a daunting task and is filled with many backhanded remarks regarding Amish communities. She comes off pompous and self-indulgent, not at all like the humbled, pious woman she paints herself out to be. Would recommend skipping this book.

Not authentic

The title of this video mentions Argentine Tango. Unfortunately, what is being taught on this tape is not authentic Argentine Tango. Not even close. It's ballroom tango. There is a huge difference: in music, style, steps, posture, etc... Don't be fooled by ballroom instructors trying to teach Argentine Tango. The only authentic instruction available on the market comes from authentic Argentine instructors from Buenos Aires.

Substitute the name "Burmese" for any cat

Although books about particular cats/pets are rare and appreciated, I'm afraid this book gave me no further insight into my Burmese cat. Perhaps I am asking too much but I expected to find a plethora of special insights into this special breed. I didn't.Especially in modern cat care I felt this book lacking. My breeders says: Fresh meat three times a week; chicken wings (raw) at least twice for dental hygiene, vary the diet, enjoy the peculiarly dog like characteristics of the Burmese. But mabe that's all asking too much - gotta go, Nero is bringing his beloved yellow wash cloth for retrieval...It is hard to criticise a book that describes the best breed of cat on earth. Let's all write one!

I played this game as soon as it dropped , but just before it did i bought and played the Mass Effect trilogy for the first time (10/10 btw) .

Imagine my surprise when many of the cool things from ME turned up in Starfield except they were not sexy or daring because ME is a game that is Adult in nature  set in space with space exploration with a very cool story spread over three huge interlocking games, In Starfield they were sanitised and pretty much designed for 10 yr olds with a weak overarching  plot full of holes that you could just ignore anyway. Yes Starfield is a sandbox and not linear like ME but the games are similar in the themes and story and Starfield whilst cool for about 5 or 6 hrs it then drops off a cliff in terms of everything that keeps you engaged in a game .

This is decent brainless fun.

Unfortunately I have nothing else positive to say about Chivalry 2.

Torn Banner is quite the hostile mess, not only to their most loyal supporters, but also to their own staff.

After abandoning Chivalry 1, their players and their staff. Torn Banner pretty much lazily remakes Chivalry 1, without the depth and the funny bits that made it special, and slaps the number 2 on it.

Chivalry 1 was glorious and Mordhau is its real successor, with even more depth, skill expression and funzies.

If you want a real medieval melee game, made by real Chivalry 1 fans, with substance and heart; Play Mordhau instead of this sloppy cashgrab.

Look. The game is incredible. Egosoft are vastly overly ambitious with the resources at hand to pull it off smoothly, however. Despite my playtime, I can't recommend this. Why? Save file corruption. I've done all the searching. Took action using all the tips reddit, steam, AI, you name it, have given me. Nothing - nothing has prevented me twice now, from losing multi hundred hour playthroughs in an instant. Some will not be bothered by this, the sandbox is what matters. And I wish I were like them, but I am not. I want the story alongside it. The missions, the changes, the feeling that what I'm doing matters. And that is failed time and time again by save file corruption.

The stories were great the illustrations were creepy, and like a lot of reviews, my little brother was scared of that picture in the haunted house story. well, ok it was pretty darn ugly. This is one of those books that still gives me the chills especially fro mthose pictures? oh what a warped mind that artist had but what creative drawings they are!Now, if you think the books are scary, try listening to the cassettes. i am in my twenties and the voice of the narrator and that creepy music gives me the willies. try listening to it in a room by yourself, and see how long it takes you to run for the door! The Scary Stories and More Scary Stories cassetes (i am not kidding) it is a kid's tape and that music will creep you out. listen to it! pick up the book follow along and see how long you last!

I bought this when it came out on Steam and have played over a hundred hours, so not nothing. It seemed so promising from the start, I really enjoyed it even though it was sort of a dead end. Since then it seems like the devs are focused on adding complexity to a game that's (understandably) broken (because its easy access) which makes no sense.

It's also been a couple years and I'm not sure that we're any closer to a complete game than we were then. I've lost interest and I'm no longer optimistic that this project will bear fruit in the form of a balanced, polished game.

I feel like the most likely outcome at this point is they fill in the rest with AI, it remains a buggy mess in production, and never feels like a finished game. Hoping I'm proved wrong.

Self-Serving Message

This is the tale of a kindly Rabbi, his sweet daughter and the cat who loves her. The tale seems promising at first, until it delves into bitterness over God and those who love Him and follow His laws. The cat represents the glorification of sin itself, and delights whenever the book's characters fall into ungodly habits, judging them forever as hypocrites (taking no account into repentance and future avoidance of said sin). As is the case with most humanist literature the story down spirals from that point until it ends with the Rabbi losing faith in God. At this point the cat is truly happy with the Rabbi, thus giving the tale a 'happy ending'. In short, 'The Rabbi's Cat' is a tale structured to appeal to secular humanists, atheists and pagans who want to feel better about their self-serving, do as you feel, lifestyles.One more note: This book, despite the beautiful artwork and appealing cover, is definitely not appropriate for children.

I'd like to say I enjoyed Return to Monkey Island and for a decent portion of it, I did. However the game is built upon two assumptions:

1. You're a Monkey Island fan.
2. You want to see the series come to a satisfying conclusion.

As such, a lot of the game is built around old tropes of the series and continuously makes references back to old jokes and events from previous titles. This is fine in and of itself but something that I found made Monkey Island 1-3 continuously interesting and fulfilling was the willingness to expand its own world and venture into new territories.

RtMI doesn't really tread any new ground aside from a few new locations in the latter half of the game. The story is pretty much beating a dead horse and hoping something exciting happens. And when nothing exciting happens we're supposed to sit back and laugh at ourselves for being so gullible as to expect the creators to do something satisfying with what is supposed to be the ultimate love letter to their series.
